title: Continuous finite quotient system of invariant partitions
statement: Use the small representatives of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be any topological group and let $P$ be a compact topological space with a continuous left action $G\times P\to P$. A finite clopen partition means a finite set of pairwise disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets with union $P$, allowing the empty partition when $P$ is empty. Let $J$ be the set of all such partitions that are permuted by $G$, equivalently the invariant discrete quotients of [def-sfb-invariant-discrete-quotients]. Order $J$ by $i\le j$ if $j$ refines $i$. Then $J$ is small, nonempty and directed, and the category $J^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered. For each $i\in J$ let $P_i$ be its finite set of blocks with discrete topology, and let $q_i:P\to P_i$ send a point to its block. For $i\le j$ let $r_{ji}:P_j\to P_i$ send a block to the unique block containing it. These are continuous surjections satisfying $r_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $r_{ki}=r_{ji}\circ r_{kj}$ for $i\le j\le k$, and $r_{ji}\circ q_j=q_i$. The formulas $g\cdot B=gB$ give continuous left actions on every $P_i$; all $q_i$ and $r_{ji}$ are $G$-equivariant. For any nonempty block $B\in P_i$, any $x_B\in B$, and $C\in P_i$, one has $gB=C$ if and only if $gx_B\in C$.

proof.text: Use the universe bound of [def-weil-size-convention]. Each partition is a subset of the power set of the small underlying set $P$, so $J$ is a subset of $\mathcal P(\mathcal P(P))$ and is small. The relation $x\sim_i y$ meaning that $x,y$ lie in the same block has precisely those blocks as its classes. The preimage of any subset of the block set is a union of open blocks, so this relation has discrete quotient topology. Conversely, classes of any discrete quotient are clopen: both a singleton and its complement in the quotient are open. The classes cover $P$; compactness gives a finite subcover, and disjointness and nonemptiness force every class to occur in it. Thus these are exactly finite clopen partitions. If $G$ permutes blocks the relation is invariant. Conversely, invariance as in [def-sfb-invariant-discrete-quotients] gives $gB\subseteq C$ for the block $C$ containing $gx$ with $x\in B$; applying invariance to $g^{-1}$ gives $g^{-1}C\subseteq B$, so $gB=C$. This verifies the equivalence of the two descriptions of the index.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion of invariant quotient partitions; Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, finite-decomposition index.

proof.text: For $P\ne\varnothing$, the one-block partition $\{P\}$ is invariant; for $P=\varnothing$, the empty partition is invariant. Given $i,j\in J$, form $k=\{B\cap C:B\in i,\ C\in j,\ B\cap C\ne\varnothing\}$. These are finitely many nonempty clopen sets. Each point belongs to exactly one of them because it belongs to exactly one block of each partition. Thus $k$ is a partition refining both. Moreover $g(B\cap C)=gB\cap gC$, since $g$ is a bijection, so $G$ permutes its blocks. Hence $k\in J$ and $J$ is nonempty and directed.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion; Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, common refinement of finite decompositions.

proof.text: Refinement is reflexive and transitive. If $i\le j\le i$, take $B\in i$ and $x\in B$. The $j$-block $C$ containing $x$ is contained in an $i$-block; that block contains $x$ and hence equals $B$. Conversely $B$ is contained in a $j$-block, which must be $C$. Thus $B=C$. Reversing the roles of $i,j$ shows that the partitions agree. In $J^{\mathrm{op}}$, a common refinement gives an object with arrows to any two objects. Parallel arrows are equal because this is a poset category and are equalized by an identity. Together with nonemptiness these are the defining cofilteredness conditions.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion; Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, directed index and cofiltered diagram.

proof.text: Each $P_i$ is finite by the definition of partition. For any subset $A\subseteq P_i$, one has $q_i^{-1}(A)=\bigcup_{B\in A}B$, an open set; thus $q_i$ is continuous into the discrete topology. For each block $B$, choose $x\in B$; then $q_i(x)=B$, proving surjectivity. The same proof covers the empty space: both source and target are empty, so surjectivity is vacuous.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion; Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, maps from the space to its finite block sets.

proof.text: For $i\le j$, a nonempty $j$-block $D$ is contained in an $i$-block by refinement, and in at most one by disjointness. This defines $r_{ji}$. For $B\in P_i$, a point $x\in B$ has a $j$-block $D$ with $r_{ji}(D)=B$, proving surjectivity. Every map between discrete spaces is continuous: the preimage of an open set is a subset of a discrete space. Uniqueness of the containing block gives $r_{ii}(B)=B$, $r_{ji}(r_{kj}(D))=r_{ki}(D)$, and $r_{ji}(q_j(x))=q_i(x)$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion; Stacks topology.tex Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, canonical refinement maps and the inverse system.

proof.text: Invariance makes $gB$ a block of the same partition. The identities $1B=B$ and $(gh)B=g(hB)$ follow by taking images under the given action, and define a left action on $P_i$. If $x_B\in B$ and $gB=C$, then $gx_B\in C$. Conversely, $gx_B\in C\cap gB$ forces $C=gB$ by disjointness of blocks. This proves the stated criterion for every choice of $x_B$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion of the finite discrete G-sets: induced block action and point criterion.

proof.text: The point $gx$ belongs to the block $gq_i(x)$, hence $q_i(gx)=gq_i(x)$. If $D\subseteq B=r_{ji}(D)$, then $gD\subseteq gB$, where $gD$ is a $j$-block and $gB$ is an $i$-block. The unique-containing-block definition therefore gives $r_{ji}(gD)=gB=g\,r_{ji}(D)$. These are exactly the two equivariance assertions.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p. 28, agent expansion of continuous equivariant maps between finite discrete G-sets.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a target block $C$. For each $B\in P_i$ choose $x_B\in B$ and put $U_{BC}=\{g\in G:gx_B\in C\}$. The map $g\mapsto(g,x_B)$ is continuous (its coordinates are the identity and a constant), so the given joint continuity of the original action and openness of $C$ show that $U_{BC}$ is open. By the criterion in step 6, the preimage of $\{C\}$ under $(g,B)\mapsto gB$ is $\bigcup_{B\in P_i}(U_{BC}\times\{B\})$, which is open in $G\times P_i$. Every subset of the discrete target is a union of singletons; its preimage is consequently open. This proves joint continuity, including the empty target, when the action map has empty domain.
